findings: The diff has no implementation. Plan step 1 was to add `subtract(a, b)` to `target/src/calc/__init__.py`, and that file is not changed.

The test in `target/tests/test_subtract.py` assigns `calc.subtract = lambda a, b: a - b` at module level. It then asserts against its own lambda, so it passes whether or not the real function exists. It would never fail first, which breaks the write-the-failing-test-first rule.
The monkeypatch also sets `calc.subtract` on the shared `calc` module at import time. That can mask a missing function in other tests and gives false confidence.
The only test is one case, `subtract(3, 1) == 2`. It covers no negative results, zero or negative inputs.
